highlights.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
highlights.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry.
body: The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military’s national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday’s mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX’s Starlink. Sunday’s failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time.

Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights.

Sunday’s launch succumbed to a different kind of failure. The six solid rocket boosters appeared to perform well in the first two minutes after Vulcan’s liftoff from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, at 12:40 pm EDT (17:40 UTC).

highlights.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
highlights.summary: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.
body: In the first guest post on our science blog, physicist Nathaniel Craig, a visiting scientist at OpenAI, describes how he worked with GPT‑6 Astra on a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model. Craig leads the particle theory group at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

I had a strategy for tackling this problem, but had not been able to prove that it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. Astra helped turn that strategy into a construction and took the lead in developing the detailed proof. To explain what we did, it helps to start with what is missing from our existing description of the Standard Model.

highlights.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
highlights.summary: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva caps her stellar season with a hard-fought victory over Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals.
body: For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament.
The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week.
The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years.
The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina.

highlights.title: Tom Cruise's Favorite Director's Breakout Action Thriller Is Officially Free to Stream
highlights.summary: As strange as it may be from a modern perspective, there was a point at which Christopher McQuarrie did not work with Tom Cruise. 20 years before McQuarrie directed four Mission: Impossible movies in a row, he got on moviegoers' radar by writing the Oscar-winning script for 1995's The Usual…
body: We don't talk quite as much about Usual Suspects as we used to, as much of it's built around a truly incredible performance by the since-disgraced Kevin Spacey, but it's one of the greatest movies in the neo-noir crime revival of the '90s. In theory, that and the Oscar should've given McQuarrie a blank check to do whatever he wanted. Instead, he was unemployed for the next five years.

Finally, McQuarrie wrote and directed his own follow-up to Usual Suspects just to put himself back on the film industry's radar. That was 2000's The Way of the Gun, which is an angry reaction to McQuarrie's years in Hollywood. It's an action movie that deliberately does everything that a film executive wouldn't want to see come across their desk, such as long silences, surprisingly subtle plot beats, and two of the most deliberately unsympathetic protagonists in American movie history. If you brought this to Kevin Zaslav, he’d spontaneously combust.

highlights.summary: Kevin Feige is celebrating 25 years of Marvel history by going back to the beginning. The Marvel Studios president, who was an associate producer on the 2000s “X-Men,” is introducing several of the original characters — including James Marsden’s Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn’s Mystique, Professor X…
body: “You see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together.’ It just felt right,” Feige told Empire in a recent interview. “It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.”
Jackman’s influence on the fifth “Avengers” film does not stop with old interview clips.

Fans spotted on Thursday that the screenwriting credits for “Doomsday” list Ryan Reynolds and Jackman among the 10 writers who contributed to the movie. The writing credits for the Deadpool and Wolverine actors give the impression that they would be for writing dialogue for their “X-Men” characters, but it’s unclear if or how much they would appear in “Doomsday.”
It has been confirmed, though, that the late Patrick Stewart will return for his final movie role in “Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles Xavier.

highlights.title: How sensitive data from Centrelink and other Australian agencies may have been fed to Palantir software
highlights.summary: Exclusive: Personal information of Centrelink clients and childcare workers is among data shared with ACIC, which uses US tech company’s software. The personal information of Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers is among a trove of sensitive data that may be ending up in Palantir’s…
body: As Guardian Australia reported in September, Palantir’s software is used by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission (ACIC) as part of the multi-agency fraud fusion taskforce, which was established in 2022 with the goal of targeting fraud in government payments from the national disability insurance scheme, childcare and welfare.

New documents, released under freedom of information requests, reveal the extent to which at least 10 government agencies share sensitive data with the taskforce, which could be fed into Palantir’s software.

The controversial US tech company, co-founded by the Donald Trump-aligned billionaire Peter Thiel, has clients including the Israeli military and US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that use the software to analyse vast amounts of data.

While the company has insisted it has no access to the data clients enter into the software, the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, has led calls for a ban on Palantir contracts with the Australian government.

highlights.title: Our new blog for science
highlights.summary: The OpenAI science blog shares new findings, practical methods, and firsthand accounts from researchers using AI to advance scientific discovery.
body: We’re starting the OpenAI science blog to give scientists and academic researchers a place to share what they’re discovering with AI and how they’re doing the work. Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity, and accelerating scientific discovery is one of the most impactful ways we can work toward that goal.
Research and discoveries: New scientific results and updates on ongoing research from OpenAI, our collaborators, and the broader scientific community.

Methods and practical guidance: Examples of how scientists use our models for tasks such as scientific computing, data analysis, exploring literature, and planning experiments. We’ll share approaches others can adapt, including how to check the work and where a method falls short.

Perspectives from the scientific community: Firsthand accounts from researchers using AI, what they are learning, and how these capabilities are affecting their disciplines. We’ll also discuss open questions about scientific practice and how to make these tools useful to more people.

highlights.title: Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final
highlights.summary: Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset. Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds. Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title. After a week dominated by a headline-grabbing stadium scheduling imbroglio, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to…
body: Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley off the crossbar and in to seal a 2-1 upset that left Gotham FC’s title defense in tatters. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the defending champions into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.

On a windswept afternoon where unyielding gusts undercut the warmth of a cloudless 50F sky, a physical opening stretch produced six fouls in the first eight minutes before either side threatened. Gotham recorded the first shot after 12 minutes when Jaedyn Shaw ran onto a Guro Reiten pass and missed wide right. Kansas City answered three minutes later, with Malawian star Temwa Chawinga firing wide left from the center of the area.

Twenty minutes in, Bethune won a free kick 25 yards out after a foul by Denise O’Sullivan. Stepping up with her left foot, she coolly curled her strike around the Gotham wall and inches inside the post. The goal from Bethune, the NWSL’s midfielder of the year two seasons ago with Washington, left the crowd in stunned silence before a smattering of boos echoed around the ground.

highlights.title: Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'
highlights.summary: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."
body: Microsoft unveiled a slew of details about its past, present, and future with the surprise publication of the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. It's all part of surprise festivities meant to help celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and it also happens to have revealed more information about Project Helix than we've received in some time.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has called the next-gen project a "family of devices" before, and although that language is used again here, vice president of next generation Jason Ronald helped paint a clearer picture. The main idea here is that, through the ups and downs of Xbox's history, many lessons have been learned.

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."
points: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."

highlights.title: F.D.A. Rejects Closely Watched Lung Cancer Drug From China
highlights.summary: This X-ray shows stage 1 cancer. Summit Therapeutics of Florida had been seeking to bring to the U.S. market a drug for lung cancer, called ivonescimab, that was invented in China.
body: The Food and Drug Administration rejected a first-of-its-kind cancer drug that was invented in China, a setback for a medicine that had become a symbol of China’s ascendance as a powerhouse in drug development.

Summit Therapeutics, the Florida company that has been seeking to bring the drug to the American market, disclosed the agency’s decision in a news release on Sunday. Summit bought the U.S. rights to the drug from Akeso Biopharma, a Chinese drugmaker that invented the drug in its laboratories and sells it in China.

Summit had been seeking approval only for certain patients with advanced lung cancer. But the drug had raised high hopes because it is being tested in many more cancers, including tumors of the colon, bladder and breast.

Summit said on Sunday that the F.D.A. told the company it had rejected the drug because it had not shown a statistically significant benefit in prolonging patients’ lives in the global clinical trial that was the basis of Summit’s application.

highlights.title: Fan Fiction Site AO3 Returns, and So Do Its Readers, in Droves
highlights.summary: The archive, which is home to tales inspired by the likes of “Harry Potter” and “Heated Rivalry,” was taken down more than two weeks ago, leaving its fans bereft.
body: It’s a library of nearly 19 million works, more than double the circulating materials of the New York Public Library, so when it was knocked offline in a “security incident” more than two weeks ago, its 12 million users were aghast.

The volunteers who run the fan fiction site AO3, short for “ Archive of Our Own,” had quickly assured its enormous community that no data — especially all those works — had been lost and that it would be restored in four weeks.

But on Sunday, the repository of homespun stories based on works like “Harry Potter,” “Twilight” and “Heated Rivalry” was mostly back online, with some features — like importing external work — temporarily disabled, to help the site return earlier than expected.
“The intensity of the response speaks to how deeply fan fiction has become woven into our lives,” Dana Bryce, a writer and cultural commentator in Toronto, said on Sunday afternoon.

highlights.title: Greaves out of Grand Slam despite win over Zonneveld
highlights.summary: Beau Greaves' win over Niels Zonneveld is in vain as she is knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts because of Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
body: Beau Greaves was eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts at the group stage despite ending her campaign with a win over Niels Zonneveld in Wolverhampton.
Greaves, 22, beat Dutchman Zonneveld 5-3 but it was not enough to keep her in the competition after Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
The three-time women's world champion fought back impressively from 3-1 down, winning three consecutive legs to take the lead in the best-of-five match.
She missed two match darts in a tense final leg but 28-year-old Zonneveld could not capitalise, failing to take out 154 before Greaves finished with double eight to seal the victory.

highlights.title: Prime Video's Near-Perfect Game of Thrones Replacement Officially Arrives in 2 Months
highlights.summary: A weak king rules over a cobbled-together kingdom that's already coming apart at the seams. Various heroes and villains compete and scheme to claim the throne. A new challenger rises up from across the sea, full of vengeance and bloodlust...
body: Back in October, during New York Comic Con 2026, I attended an early screening of Bloodaxe, a new series from Vikings creator Michael Hirst and his son Horatio. Based on the show's first episode, which premieres Jan. 20, 2027 on Prime Video, the streamer might just have a new Game of Thrones -level hit on its hands. Or at the very least, an entertaining show for VIkings fans.

That might sound like a lot of plot to pack into one hour of television, and… it is. But Michael and Horatio Hirst deftly plunge us into this world headfirst like a Viking warrior sprinting into the frigid Norwegian Sea. Like Game of Thrones, Bloodaxe pulls out all the stops in its opening act to win over its audience. That means plenty of political intrigue, shocking deaths, stunning scenery, meticulous production design, beautiful actors, and gratuitous sex scenes.

highlights.title: The Jensen Huang Scandal Has Shocked Even Scandal-Prone Silicon Valley
highlights.summary: As Jensen Huang abruptly departs, the tech community grapples with an eternal question: Why do the smartest and most successful men so often act so stupidly?
body: Artificial intelligence promises transcendence. We will ditch our tired and inefficient bodies, say farewell to tedious work and trips to the grocery store. The computer will tend to all human needs and solve all human problems.

Well, that was the idea. A.I. was supposed to achieve a new level of reality this month with the public sale of shares of Anthropic, one of the two start-ups that have created and defined this young industry. A trillion-dollar company will be born, yielding billionaires galore.

A.I. is the biggest Silicon Valley story ever. But last Sunday it was suddenly pushed aside when the chief executive of the company whose chips are literally powering this intelligence revolution confessed to cheating on his wife with a woman, Alice Huang, who U.S. officials believe was spying for China. By Thursday morning he had resigned, something few thought possible just days earlier.

The scandal that took down Nvidia chief Jensen Huang is full of implications for national security and the global A.I. boom. Mr. Huang ranked among Mark Zuckerberg, Steve Jobs, Elon Musk and Bill Gates as tech leaders who were considered by the world to be inseparable from the companies they built.

highlights.summary: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips.
body: Following revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy Congress wants to crack down.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.

Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

highlights.title: LeBron James now third in all-time NBA assists
highlights.summary: LeBron James had 11 assists and moved into third on the NBA's career list, as he added 15 points and six rebounds to lead the Philadelphia 76ers past the Indiana Pacers 131-124 on Sunday.
body: James, who turns 42 next month, dished one to VJ Edgecombe in the fourth quarter for assist 12,092 to pass Jason Kidd on the career list. John Stockton and Chris Paul are No 1 and 2 in NBA history.
James continued an early habit in his first season with the Sixers in picking his spot to take control of a game.

This one came in the third quarter, right after Sixers fans went wild when seldom-used 7-foot-6 center Tacko Fall checked into the game. James immediately went to work picking apart the Pacers and scored eight straight points to give them an 82-73 lead.

Fall helped in that pivotal third quarter stretch for James. Fall grabbed an offensive rebound that led to a possession where James would sink two from the free-throw line. James then added a near-uncontested driving layup because of a perfect screen from Fall. James added a 20-footer and a dunk during the run.

highlights.title: Xbox Reveals Original and 360 Boot-Up Options for 25th Anniversary
highlights.summary: Microsoft has revealed three new nostalgic Xbox console boot-up options for Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One as part of a new update for the brand's 25th anniversary. Xbox has been around a long time, and those who have stuck around for the full ride have seen it through plenty of ups and downs.
body: These three new animations are largely untouched rips of the same boot-up videos from some of the earliest days of Microsoft's gaming endeavors. The Original is the same sci-fi-inspired introduction that played for original Xbox consoles. The other two options are Xbox 360-themed, with one being based on the 2005 startup and the other based on the 2010 startup.

Xbox has been going hard on the nostalgia to help celebrate its 25th anniversary today. In addition to the three new boot-up animations, Microsoft published the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, which offered a full layout for the company's 25-year history in games and what's coming next.

Part of the future includes plotting ahead for Project Helix, a project the company has previously described as a family of devices that could mark a new path forward for Xbox. It all arrives as Microsoft navigates a tough year for the brand, which has seen it introduce a new CEO in Asha Sharma and announce thousands of layoffs.

highlights.title: ‘I Love Being a Girl’: Inside the Life of a Sorority Influencer
highlights.summary: Many young adults want to be influencers. And why not? It’s fun. But it also means that the camera is always on.
body: The Alpha Phi sorority house at the University of Arizona occupies a professionally decorated Spanish colonial-style mansion just off campus. There’s a chandeliered dining room, two pink-and-baby-blue living rooms and a tanning area on the roof.

It’s where Haley DeKreek, a 20-year-old junior, lives with her closest friends. It’s also the backdrop to her budding career. Her work takes place mostly in her room, but she picks up the rewards in the mailroom just off the foyer.

Perpetually suffused with floral perfume, it overflows with packages, many of them hers: boxes with dresses for formals or matching yoga sets, boxes of makeup, hair products and skin care. Some she ordered herself, but many are freebies from brands that have spotted her potential as a TikTok influencer, a one-girl campus marketing powerhouse. Nearly all are destined to appear in the many-stepped “get ready with me” videos she has posted since she was a first-year student rushing sororities.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.

highlights.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
highlights.summary: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
body: Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

highlights.title: Mirra Andreeva holds nerve against Svitolina to win WTA Finals for first time
highlights.summary: Andreeva seals 7-5, 6-3 victory to earn world No 2 ranking. Russian dominates tournament without losing a set. Mirra Andreeva had put herself on the brink of securing another effortless, straightforward set in one of the biggest finals of her career when she momentarily balked.
body: There have already been many times in Andreeva’s young career when similar sequences triggered epic, dramatic collapses, so prone the 19-year-old has been to losing her composure when things do not go her way. This time, she betrayed no negative emotions at all. Andreeva immediately retrieved the break and regained her momentum as she marched to a monumental victory, defeating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win the WTA Finals at Indian Wells for the first time.

This is the perfect end to a year in which Andreeva won her first grand slam title at Roland Garros and established herself as one of the leading players of her generation. She will rise to a new high ranking of No 2 and she will sit just 293 points behind Elena Rybakina, who starts her 2027 season by attempting to defend the Australian Open title. Andreeva has put herself in the perfect position to attack the No 1 ranking at the beginning of the year.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Billy Idol Rebels, Phil Collins Gets Emotional and Rick Rubin Clones Invade the Rock Hall Induction Ceremony
highlights.summary: Chris Rock roasted Diddy, Jack Black toasted Iron Maiden's no-show and Gwen Stefani sang with her teenage idol as the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction turned into a glorious, generation-scrambling mess.
body: Rick Rubin summed up the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony in one line: “You can’t kill rock ‘n’ roll.”
Fair enough, given how many people onstage Saturday night have spent the past half-century testing that theory.
And then there were the Red Hot Chili Peppers, who showed up dressed as Rubin.

Big white beards, balding white wigs, orange-tinted shades: the band turned themselves into a squad of Rubin clones and tore through “Give It Away,” the hit from Blood Sugar Sex Magik, the first album he made with them. Chad Smith’s bass drum carried a portrait of the man himself. It was the most gloriously ridiculous sight of the night, and proof that the Peppers can still act like the guys who once played shows in strategically placed socks.

highlights.title: Use Humor to Defuse Awkward Moments
highlights.summary: If you can laugh at yourself, other people will feel more at ease around you, experts say.
body: Recently, running late for my train to work, I bolted from the house without using my hair-in-a-can. That’s the sprayable hair color I use between dye jobs.

I arrived at the office with snow-white tufts on my temples. Rather than trying to avoid my co-workers, I thought back to a study I’d read about earlier this year. Researchers had found that when someone made a harmless misstep in public, and then laughed at their own blunder, others saw them as warmer and more authentic.
So when I made it to work, I set the tone right away by announcing that I was aware of my temple tufts and of my resemblance to Paulie Walnuts of “The Sopranos.”

“When you can laugh at yourself, that signals that you have some self-acceptance,” said Ovul Sezer Peck, an assistant professor of management and organizations at Cornell University and an author of that study, which was published in The Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. “You’re showing people that you’re comfortable with yourself and your imperfections, which makes you more relatable.”

highlights.title: Listen to this: Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders
highlights.summary: I open with this caveat: I haven't had a ton of time to digest the surprise Armand Hammer record that dropped this week. Billy Woods and Elucid rarely miss, though, and my initial reaction is that Snakes & Ladders ranks among their best.
body: Ominous noises dance in the background, blasts of noise add dashes of industrial rage, bass lines throb, and saxophone bleats call out to the sky. Woods and Elucid have always had excellent taste in production, but here they seem to have brought out the best in collaborators like clipping, Kenny Segal, and Child Actor. They’ve also successfully rallied them around a specific sound palette that keeps the record from actually sounding like it has beats from 11 different producers.

Of course, what makes Armand Hammer stand out from many of their contemporaries is their unique and verbose flows. Their lyrical mastery even makes guest rappers like $ilkmoney, who you can practically hear stalking around the mic as he seethes on “Risk,” up their game.
On songs like “Gravity,” Billy Woods navigates burgeoning romance with shocking directness, while also acknowledging obliquely how hard it can be to say what you mean.
On “Vespers,” he references Siouxsie and the Banshees and says “My nightcap three fingers of Fernet,” which is probably the first time I’ve ever heard Fernet Branca get a shoutout in a rap song.

highlights.title: SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft
highlights.summary: While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week’s episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once.
body: In a single sketch, we got James Austin Johnson as Peter Thiel, Ben Marshall as Sam Altman, Jane Wickline as Dario Amodei, Jeremy Culhane as Elon Musk, Andrew Dismukes as Mark Zuckerberg — and eventually, the recently departed Bowen Yang joined the fun as Jensen Huang.

Huang’s ouster from Nvidia (after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy) could have serious implications for the tech industry; it also provided a hook for some obvious jokes about rich nerds being easy marks for women (or men) who are out of their league.

In the sketch, a CIA agent played by host John Mulaney (hilarious as ever, if not entirely confident about how to pronounce “Palantir” or “Nvidia”) attempts to painstakingly explain why these execs should be suspicious when someone attractive suddenly seems interested in them romantically. For Altman and Thiel’s sake, he added, “I hope this is obvious: Even though you’re gay, you can still be tricked by a spy.”

highlights.title: 17 Years Ago, the Longest Running Sci-Fi Show Flipped Its Core Concept On Its Head
highlights.summary: If there’s one thing you can’t say about Tennant, it’s that he lacks range. He can play a lover, a fighter, or the scummiest person you know. But his most iconic role as the time-traveling alien known as the Doctor in the sci-fi family show Doctor Who brings all three together.
body: David Tennant has long been recognized as one of the greatest actors alive. He’s played scoundrels, cops, serial killers, and even a demon — an actual one, not a member of the Conservative Party, though he’s played one of those too.

That might be a shocking statement to process. One of the Doctor’s core moral philosophies, articulated as early as Classic Who in 1963, is that the Time Lord is ultimately a peaceful person. During the Twelfth Doctor’s (Peter Capaldi) regeneration in 2017, one of his very last statements was that the future Doctor should “never be cruel, never be cowardly, and never ever eat pears! Remember, hate is always foolish, but love is always wise. Always try to be nice, but never fail to be kind.”
And yet, Tennant’s Tenth Doctor was the opposite of all those things during the 2009 autumnal Doctor Who special, "The Waters of Mars."
There have always been moments when the Doctor has shown that, for every person he has saved over the centuries, there have been just as many whom he has condemned.

highlights.title: A Deep Dive Into Hailey Bieber’s Many, Many Face Masks
highlights.summary: From cult K-beauty treatments to depuffing creams, collagen wraps, and LED light therapy, Rhode founder Hailey Bieber takes her masking seriously.
body: “Dealing with my issues one mask a time,” wrote Hailey Bieber beneath a recent Instagram carousel. While she’s not elaborating on said issues, her extensive collection of face masks have been exposed for every skincare obsessive’s over-analysis. Hailey Bieber has a face mask for every occasion and skin concern, it seems.

There she is, covered in mustard-yellow paste, slathered in a thick white cream, encased in a glossy lavender-grey treatment, and illuminated by the electric-blue glow of an LED device. There are hydrogel sheets, eye patches, and a rather arresting cobalt-blue mask from a recent trip to Seoul. Bieber is clearly not afraid to cast the net wide in pursuit of good skin.

As she’s previously explained, her approach when her skin is irritated is minimal: rinsing with water, using prescribed azelaic acid and clindamycin, hypochlorous acid, and Rhode’s ceramide-rich Glazing Milk. In her 2025 Beauty Secrets video, she also revealed that she generally skips a full morning cleanse in favor of a water rinse, saving the heavier-duty moisturizing for nighttime.

Jaylen Brown contributed a team-high 31 points to go with 3 three pointers 2 rebounds and 2 assists, with Tyrese Maxey of the 76ers adding an additional 27 points (9-19 FG, 5-10 3P) in the game.
Pascal Siakam finished with a team-high 31 points along with 2 rebounds for the Pacers in the losing effort.
